title: THIS SEAT HAS A HEAD.
subtitle: A pillion-seat media intervention for adult two-wheeler users
selected_cause: Pillion helmet use on everyday two-wheeler journeys
user_selection: A and C accepted; user leans towards C. C developed as lead; A retained as cause-level runner-up.
audience: Adult student and early-career driver–pillion pairs aged 18–30, encountered while stationary in a permissioned campus or residential parking area.
audience_status: Strategic focus, not a measured population segment or a claimed local prevalence finding.
objective: Prompt both adults on a shared two-wheeler ride to wear their own suitable helmet and fasten its chinstrap before departure.
insight: On an ordinary shared ride, the second seat can become an afterthought. Make the reminder appear where the second person is about to sit.
insight_status: Creative hypothesis informed by published evidence; not a verbatim participant quote or a validated local finding.
proposition: The person on the second seat needs their own helmet too.

seat_card: Pillion passengers need a helmet too.
Put on and fasten your helmet before you ride.
poster: Riding together? Check each other before you leave.
Use a well-fitting BIS-certified motorcycle helmet.
social: Both helmets on. Both straps fastened.
Check before you ride. Never while riding.

visual_system.type: Helvetica / Helvetica Bold in PDFs; Arial / system sans in HTML
visual_system.art_direction: Bold paired helmet illustrations, large type, plain language, generous space. No crash imagery, police styling, fake fine, invented endorsement or logo artwork.

concepts.name: The second-seat message
concepts.medium: Existing stationary pillion seat used as a temporary advertising placement
concepts.mechanism: An A6 campaign card rests on the rear seat during a supervised, opt-in stationary encounter. The seat identifies the relevant passenger without a scan or device.
concepts.reason: Closest relationship between overlooked passenger, physical placement and immediate pre-ride action; modest prototype requirements.
concepts.limits: Weather, attention, consent and collection must be controlled; do not leave cards on unattended vehicles or allow mounting before removal.

concepts.name: The two-person parking slip
concepts.mechanism: Turn a one-vehicle record into a two-person reminder.
concepts.reason: A documented HDFC Bank/STUDDS Helmet Receipt campaign already uses receipt-style slips. Avoid a close executional precedent, mock fines and implied enforcement.
concepts.limits: Not claimed to be identical; similarity makes it a weaker originality choice for this project.

concepts.name: The plus-one ride invite
concepts.medium: Existing direct-message image or social Story before a planned ride
concepts.mechanism: A paired visual makes the passenger part of ride planning: 'Bringing someone? Bring both helmets.' No new app, bot or platform integration.
concepts.reason: Easy to prototype and useful as reinforcement, but more distant from the mounting decision and easier to ignore as generic content.
concepts.limits: No evidence that the audience plans rides through this format; use only before riding, not while moving.

research.title: Factors associated with nonuse of helmet among motorcyclists sustaining road traffic accidents
research.finding: Hospital-based observational sample of 346 adult crash patients in eastern India; 35.7% used helmets; 334 (96.6%) agreed helmets were essential. Short-distance travel and forgetfulness were associated with nonuse; pillion status was also associated with nonuse.
research.limit: Consecutive hospital sample, not representative of India, Mumbai, all young people or uninjured commuters. Observational association is not causation. Do not misread the share of helmet users who were pillions as a pillion compliance rate.
research.verification: Primary article found through search and publisher full text inspected; both locations represent the same study, not independent replication.

research.title: Road Accidents in India 2024: safety-device data
research.anchor: OpenCity records: Category=Passenger, No Helmet - Killed=14,652; Category=Total, No Helmet - Killed=54,122; MoRTH report Table 3.3 / Annexure 37
research.finding: 14,652 passenger fatalities and 54,122 total fatalities were recorded in the non-wearing-of-helmet category in 2024.
research.limit: MoRTH data reproduced by a third-party portal and matching news reporting; original ministry table cells not directly inspected in this run. Not proof nonuse caused the crash or that every death was preventable. No Mumbai, short-trip or age-specific inference.
research.use: Attributed national context in the research section only; excluded from short public artwork
research.verification: Reproduced table cells inspected via OpenCity API and cross-checked with reporting; both derive from MoRTH, not independent datasets.

research.title: Road traffic injuries
research.data_period: WHO current fact sheet; underlying studies vary
research.anchor: Risk factors: non-use of motorcycle helmets; safe-system approach
research.finding: WHO states correct helmet use can reduce death risk by more than six times and brain-injury risk by up to 74%. Road safety also requires safe roads, speeds, vehicles and post-crash care.
research.limit: General evidence, not a prediction of this campaign's impact or a guarantee of protection; exact efficacy figures are not used in artwork.
research.use: Support safety rationale without implying helmets prevent all crashes
research.verification: WHO page inspected; PIB repeats WHO statement, not an independent efficacy study.

research.title: Helmet — More Than Just a Shell
research.anchor: Choose Smart. Ride Safe. Use BIS-Certified Helmets; IS 4151:2015
research.finding: Government guidance promotes BIS-certified motorcycle helmets conforming to IS 4151:2015; retention and chinstrap performance matter.
research.limit: Do not reproduce a BIS/ISI mark as endorsement, make blanket legal claims about exemptions, or certify actual equipment from its appearance.
research.use: Public copy recommends well-fitting BIS-certified motorcycle helmets
research.verification: PIB guidance inspected; BIS product-manual search result corroborates standard identity.

research.title: STUDDS Accessories and HDFC Bank launch The Helmet Receipt campaign
research.finding: An existing campaign uses symbolic helmet receipts.
research.limit: Precedent screening is not exhaustive and is not legal clearance or proof that the selected seat-card concept is globally original.
research.use: Reject receipt concept; exclude mock fines and police simulation
research.verification: Two published reports found; campaign descriptions are reporting, not independent impact evaluations.

empirical_limits: No guaranteed originality or legal clearance
No chart-certified score or fully validated solver execution
budget_status: Planning assumptions, not vendor quotations; excludes labour, travel, permissions, tax changes and helmet purchase.

milestones.output: Cause, data/insight and three media concepts

deployment_rule: Permissioned private parking only. Owner and participant opt-in; adults only; engine off; no adhesive, fastening, vehicle alteration or unattended placement. Facilitator removes and accounts for every card before anyone mounts. No traffic intervention, enforcement role or claim of safety certification. If these conditions cannot be met, show the supplied illustrated mockup without deploying.
public_claim_policy: Campaign asks for helmet use; it does not guarantee safety, claim government/brand endorsement or imply a helmet replaces the rest of road safety.
